REQUEST: plan the episode for the module «Life detectives: what is alive?» of «Life detectives»: 3 chapters — 1.1 «The signs of life», 1.2 «From cell to organism», 1.3 «Run the investigation» — then the rally.

=== THE SERIES BIBLE (the same in every episode) ===
CAST — use these ids:
- "hero" — {child} (the learner; write exactly "{child}"): the learner: curious, brave, says what they think, sometimes wrong
- "friend" — {friend} (the learner types the name; write exactly "{friend}"): best friend: funny, jumps to conclusions, loves riddles
- "mentor" — Kaboré: the science teacher: patient, asks questions back, loves his microscope
- "family" — Mariam: the hero's grandmother: sells fruit at Rood Woko market, teases kindly
- "margo" — Margo: the AI tutor: a cheerful margouillat who whispers hints, never answers
PLACES — use these ids:
- "rood_woko_market" — Rood Woko market / Le marché Rood Woko: a busy covered market in Ouagadougou, stalls of mangoes, baskets and fabrics, warm morning light
- "courtyard" — Grandma's courtyard / La cour de Mamie: a family courtyard with a big néré tree, clay walls, a wooden bench and cooking pots
- "classroom" — The classroom / La classe: a bright primary classroom, green chalkboard, wooden desks, a microscope on the teacher's table
- "school_garden" — The school garden / Le jardin de l'école: a small school garden with rows of bean plants, a big mango tree and a watering can
- "science_fair" — The science fair / La foire scientifique: a school yard set with tables, colourful posters and bunting for a science fair
- "tanghin_dam" — Tanghin dam / Le barrage de Tanghin: the shore of a calm reservoir at sunset, reeds, a dirt path and a few fishing boats
LOCAL DETAILS you may use:
- Rood Woko is the central market of Ouagadougou.
- Ouagadougou has reservoirs, such as the one at Tanghin.
- Néré seeds are fermented to make soumbala.
- Grandma Mariam's stall has the sweetest mangoes.
THE BIBLE'S MISSION FOR THIS MODULE (a seed: sharpen it into a premise with a want, stakes and a clock): "Find out which treasures in Grandma's basket are alive before Friday's science fair" / "Découvrir quels trésors du panier de Mamie sont vivants avant la foire scientifique de vendredi"

=== FACT SHEETS — the facts to plan with, NOT the plot ===
Never use these names, which belong to the lessons' own examples: Aminata, Bouaké.
LESSON 1.1 «The signs of life» → chapter 1
  IDEA 1: Living things react to what happens around them: a mimosa folds its leaves when touched.
  IDEA 2: Living things feed, grow and reproduce: a néré seed becomes a tree that makes new seeds.
  IDEA 3: All living things are made of one or more cells; a pebble has none.
  KEY FACTS: 1. React, feed, grow, reproduce: the signs of life. 2. Every living thing is made of cells.
LESSON 1.2 «From cell to organism» → chapter 2
  IDEA 1: The cell is the smallest unit of life: it is alive on its own.
  IDEA 2: Similar cells form tissues, and tissues together form organs such as a leaf or a heart.
  IDEA 3: Organs work together in systems, and the systems make a whole organism.
  KEY FACTS: 1. Cell, tissue, organ, system, organism.
LESSON 1.3 «Run the investigation» → chapter 3
  IDEA 1: Science starts by observing something and asking a clear question about it.
  IDEA 2: A hypothesis is a possible explanation, based on what you observed, that you can test.
  IDEA 3: A fair experiment changes only one thing and keeps the rest the same, then compares the results.
  KEY FACTS: 1. Observe, ask, guess wisely, test one change.



=== COURSE QUESTIONS (ref · question → correct answer; their wording is fixed) ===
[q1] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Which of these is a sign that something is alive?» → «It reacts to what happens around it»
[q2] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «What does a mimosa leaf do when you touch it?» → «It folds shut»
[q3] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Why is a pebble not alive?» → «It never feeds, grows or reproduces»
[q4] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «What is the smallest unit of life?» → «The cell»
[q5] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «What do many similar cells working together form?» → «A tissue»
[q6] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «The heart, the lungs and the stomach are...» → «Organs»
[q7] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «What is a hypothesis?» → «An explanation you can test»
[q8] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «In a fair experiment, how many things do you change at a time?» → «Only one»
[q9] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «What is the first step of a scientific investigation?» → «Observing something»
[q10] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Which of these is NOT alive?» → «A pebble»
[q11] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Which list goes from the smallest level of life to the biggest?» → «Cell, tissue, organ, organism»
[q12] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «A fair test shows your hypothesis was wrong. What do you do?» → «Write a new hypothesis and test it»

- "beats": 1 to 4 per chapter; every IDEA of a lesson is in exactly one beat of its own chapter.
- "discovery" at most 90 characters; "title" and "card_title" at most 40; catchphrases at most 50.
- "place": a place id of the bible. "cast": 2 or 3 cast ids, "hero" always among them. Margo speaks only in a beat whose "cast" lists "margo" (2 or 3 ids with her).

- Every "paper_task" is one short task done on paper that the story needs.
- chapters[k].opens_on picks up chapters[k-1].ends_on; the rally's opens_on picks up the last chapter's ends_on.

"en" and "fr" are the name tag: a short noun with its article, at most 4 words and 40 characters ("the jar", "le bocal"), never a description ("le bocal fermé avec quelque chose de gris" is wrong).

=== FACT SHEETS — the facts to plan with, NOT the plot ===
Never use these names, which belong to the lessons' own examples: Aminata, Bouaké.
LESSON 1.1 «Les signes du vivant» → chapter 1
  IDEA 1: Le vivant réagit à ce qui se passe autour de lui : le mimosa referme ses feuilles quand on le touche.
  IDEA 2: Le vivant se nourrit, grandit et se reproduit : une graine de néré devient un arbre qui fait de nouvelles graines.
  IDEA 3: Tous les êtres vivants sont faits d'une ou de plusieurs cellules ; un caillou n'en a aucune.
  KEY FACTS: 1. Réagir, se nourrir, grandir, se reproduire : les signes du vivant. 2. Tout être vivant est fait de cellules.
LESSON 1.2 «De la cellule à l'organisme» → chapter 2
  IDEA 1: La cellule est la plus petite unité du vivant : elle vit à elle seule.
  IDEA 2: Des cellules semblables forment des tissus, et des tissus ensemble forment des organes comme une feuille ou un cœur.
  IDEA 3: Les organes travaillent ensemble en systèmes, et les systèmes forment un organisme entier.
  KEY FACTS: 1. Cellule, tissu, organe, système, organisme.
LESSON 1.3 «Mène l'enquête» → chapter 3
  IDEA 1: La science commence par observer quelque chose et poser une question claire à son sujet.
  IDEA 2: Une hypothèse est une explication possible, fondée sur ce qu'on a observé, que l'on peut tester.
  IDEA 3: Une expérience juste ne change qu'une chose, garde le reste pareil, puis compare les résultats.
  KEY FACTS: 1. Observer, demander, supposer avec soin, tester un seul changement.



=== COURSE QUESTIONS (ref · question → correct answer; their wording is fixed) ===
[q1] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Lequel de ces signes montre qu'une chose est vivante ?» → «Elle réagit à ce qui se passe autour»
[q2] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Que fait une feuille de mimosa quand on la touche ?» → «Elle se referme»
[q3] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Pourquoi un caillou n'est-il pas vivant ?» → «Il ne se nourrit, ne grandit et ne se reproduit jamais»
[q4] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Quelle est la plus petite unité du vivant ?» → «La cellule»
[q5] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Que forment de nombreuses cellules semblables qui travaillent ensemble ?» → «Un tissu»
[q6] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Le cœur, les poumons et l'estomac sont...» → «Des organes»
[q7] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Qu'est-ce qu'une hypothèse ?» → «Une explication que l'on peut tester»
[q8] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Dans une expérience juste, combien de choses changes-tu à la fois ?» → «Une seule»
[q9] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Quelle est la première étape d'une enquête scientifique ?» → «Observer quelque chose»
[q10] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Lequel de ces éléments n'est PAS vivant ?» → «Un caillou»
[q11] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Quelle liste va du plus petit niveau du vivant au plus grand ?» → «Cellule, tissu, organe, organisme»
[q12] (quiz 1.5, covers lessons 1.1–1.3) «Un test juste montre que ton hypothèse était fausse. Que fais-tu ?» → «Écrire une nouvelle hypothèse et la tester»
